# CLAUDE

<!-- BEGIN KIT-MANAGED CONTRACT -->
<!-- Generated by Kit from its universal contract. Edit project guidance outside this block. -->

This repository is managed by Kit. The rules below are invariants for every task. Contextual rules under `docs/references/rules/` hold detailed procedures; read one only when its trigger below applies. Project facts live in project memory, not here.

Precedence: `docs/CONSTITUTION.md`, then this contract and contextual rules, then feature specs, then chat. Repository rules outrank generic agent, plugin, or tool defaults. A direct human pause, hold, or revocation stops the affected action until the human resumes it.

## Project Memory

- `docs/CONSTITUTION.md` holds project invariants; `docs/specs/<feature>/SPEC.md` holds material feature rationale; `docs/references/` holds reusable project knowledge, including `docs/references/testing.md` for validation commands.
- Before implementing, inspect the relevant code and memory. When a change carries rationale that code and tests cannot preserve (behavior, architecture, contracts, rejected alternatives), create or adopt its spec with `kit spec <feature>` before editing implementation files and keep its decisions current. Otherwise create no spec and state `repository memory: not required` once in the final response.
- After validation, curate durable truth into the right document. Historical specs are evidence, not instructions. Transcripts are never repository memory.

## Changes And Delivery

- Treat the clone's primary checkout as read-only for agent work, whatever its branch or cleanliness. Make every repository change (code, tests, docs, specs, generated files, configuration) in a linked worktree at `~/worktrees/<owner>/<repository>/GH-<issue>` on branch `GH-<issue>`, created from the freshly fetched default branch, and deliver it through a ready pull request.
- Default to a new human-assigned issue, branch, worktree, and ready pull request without asking. Continue an existing lane only when the user explicitly directs it for the same work. Repair of an exact existing pull request (review, CI, base refresh, conflicts, ordered merges) reuses that pull request's head branch and never opens a coordinating or corrective pull request. Never ask the user to choose between lanes; ask only when implementation intent or a named target is materially ambiguous.
- If the primary checkout holds changes you did not make through a gated lane, preserve them: do not stage, commit, push, stash, reset, clean, discard, or transfer them. The only exception is command-owned leftovers after their matching worktree pull request has merged, handled by `delivery`.
- Never commit directly to the default or a protected branch, force-push, rewrite pushed history, delete branches to clear a lane, or bypass branch protection, reviews, required checks, or merge queues.
- Never stage secrets or `.env` files, and never print secret values.

## Authorship

- Only the human user is author, committer, and assignee. Never add agent co-author trailers, "generated with" credits, or bot identities to commits, issues, pull requests, or comments. Assign every created or reused issue and pull request to the human, for example with `--assignee @me` after confirming the authenticated `gh` account is the human's. Stop if the git identity is not the human's.

## Approval Boundaries

- Merge is its own boundary. Merge only under explicit human authorization for the scope; a bounded standing grant also covers later in-scope pull requests and new heads, so never request exact-head reauthorization. Merge only a current `MERGE_READY` head: required checks and reviews passed on that head; pending, missing, skipped, or stale evidence is not passing. A merge is not deployment or production evidence.
- Before mutating cloud, Kubernetes, or infrastructure-as-code resources, configuration, or state, or IAM, network, KMS or secrets, or persistent data and schemas: present one outline of targets, actions, impact and risk, rollback, and validation; get one explicit approval; then execute that batch without per-command prompts. Deleting infrastructure always needs that confirmation. Deploying an already-merged artifact through an existing standard workflow to already-provisioned resources is routine under standing authority.
- An unqualified "delete" means a recoverable soft delete. A hard delete (purge, force delete, history rewrite, backup deletion, irreversible cascade) requires presenting the exact targets, environment, and loss, then a specific human confirmation of those targets; re-confirm if the targets change. Initial requests and plan approval do not count.
- Slack is read-only by default. A draft is not a send. Post, reply, react, edit, or delete only after showing the exact content and receiving explicit approval for that specific action; approval is single-use.
- Ask before any other outward-facing or irreversible action that is not already authorized.
- When `.kit.yaml` enables AWS, run `kit aws verify` before the first AWS-dependent command and again before any AWS mutation, use the verified profile and Region explicitly, stop on a mismatch, and never fall back to other credentials.

## Engineering

- When `.kit.yaml` sets `source_file_line_limit`, keep handwritten source and test files within it and split by responsibility; `kit check --project` enforces it.
- Preserve language-native tests and pull-request checks; end-to-end suites supplement them. Run the project's validation before calling work complete, and fix relevant failures.
- Parallelize independent investigation when it helps. Delegated agents never mutate Git or GitHub and never write overlapping files concurrently; the primary agent owns integration, validation, and the final report.
- Resolve in-scope problems autonomously until the goal is complete or a genuine blocker remains; use current evidence to choose safe, bounded recovery.

## Reporting

- Report each check as observed. Never present a pending, skipped, unavailable, or unrun check as passing; keep literal states such as `PENDING` and `UNKNOWN`. Distinguish verified facts from inferences.
- Say plainly whether the work is finished, partly finished, blocked, or failed; keep blockers and unfinished scope as prominent as successes; state what the reader must do next.
- Include the identifiers (issue, branch, pull request, commit, deployed version) needed to find or undo every change.

## Contextual Rules

Read the named file under `docs/references/rules/` when its trigger applies; skip it otherwise.

- Creating an issue, branch, worktree, commit, push, or pull request, or repairing a pull request: `delivery.md`.
- Any merge or merge-queue action: `github-pr-merge.md`.
- Following a release or deployment, including a missing or failed pipeline: `deployment-recovery.md`.
- Mint adoption, releases, deployments, environment state, hotfix, roll-forward or rollback: `mint-deployment-lifecycle.md` when the project uses Mint.
- Adding tests, configuring CI, or end-to-end, browser, or production validation: `testing-and-environment-validation.md`.
- Backend routes, services, repositories, or adapters: `backend-service-architecture.md`; frontend routes, state flows, or components: `frontend-application-architecture.md`.
- Designing deletion or deleting persistent state: `deletion-safety.md`.
- Infrastructure mutations or deployments: `infrastructure-change-approval.md`; AWS work: `aws-agent-toolkit-guidance.md`.
- Any Slack write, or investigating a Slack link: `slack-read-only.md`.
- Delegating to subagents: `agent-team-orchestration.md`.
- Plans spanning repositories with dependent deliverables or staged activation: `cross-repository-program-coordination.md`.
- The user explicitly declares a real deadline: `deadline-mode.md`.
- Curating the Constitution: `constitution-curation.md`.
- Agent-authored responses, plans, progress updates, review findings, and completion reports: apply `asd-ste100.md` by default. Explicit user language, tone, or style requests override this writing default only.
- Optional rules added with `kit rules add` declare their own triggers in their `Applies When` section.
